payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce negative-electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism. Following an independent audit, the governing cycle-life figure is 8,400; the earlier 12,000 claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge data. The prototype’s confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. At projected 500 MWh manufacturing scale, its stack-level cost is $61/kWh. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the thalliline dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte.
